episode.title: Paris Turned The Eiffel Tower Into A Farm

synopsis: The Eiffel Tower has become the frame of a vertical farm and the whole city is terraced in green, with a market running at the tower's feet.
caption:
Paris, 2512. The city turned itself into farmland, one terrace at a time.

Nobody left. They planted the boulevards, the roofs, and finally the tower.

The Eiffel lattice is a growing frame now, and the crop comes down on hoists to the market on the Champ de Mars. The old street plan is still exactly where it was.

A fictional future, created with AI.

What would you grow on your level?

Paris, 2512. La ville s'est transformee en terres agricoles, terrasse apres terrasse.

Personne n'est parti. Ils ont plante les boulevards, puis les toits, et enfin la tour.

La charpente de fer de la Tour Eiffel est devenue une serre verticale. La recolte descend par treuils jusqu'au marche du Champ de Mars. L'ancien plan des rues n'a pas bouge.

Un futur fictif, cree avec l'IA.

Que cultiveriez-vous a votre etage ?
music: A single sustained sub-bass drone at one steady level for the whole duration, built from deep low-frequency air and distant structural resonance. It holds the same volume from the first second to the last, stays free of percussion, rhythm, melody, vocals and high frequencies, and ends mid-tone so the loop is seamless.

shots.prompt:
Shot 1, exactly 4 seconds at 24 fps, AERIAL. The camera flies high in the open sky, far ABOVE every rooftop, tower, dome and canopy in the city, and looks DOWN on it from there. The whole adapted city lies below the camera and spreads across the frame from edge to edge; the horizon and open sky sit in the top third. Think satellite, helicopter or drone at altitude. The very first frame already contains BOTH the real city's recognisable landmark or skyline AND the full extent of what was built to keep it liveable, so a viewer who sees only this one frame already knows which city it is and what happened to it. One slow, single-direction camera move only, a straight descent or a forward glide, and the camera stays above the structures for the entire four seconds. Keep the camera outdoors and airborne throughout: ground level, street level, interiors, and any position beneath a roof, canopy, bridge or shelter belong to shot 2. No pan, orbit, whip, cut or scene reset inside the shot, and no setup, approach or delayed reveal.

A high aerial view looking straight down over Paris from far above the rooftops. Every boulevard and roof is terraced into planted green levels that follow the old Haussmann street pattern exactly, and the Seine runs as a clear band through the green city. The Eiffel Tower stands at the centre of the frame with its iron lattice filled in by stacked growing decks dense with foliage from base to summit. The Arc de Triomphe reads as a hub of radiating planted avenues. The city fills the frame to every edge with sky across the top third. The camera descends slowly and straight down for the full duration on one heading, staying above the tower, so the terraces resolve into rows and the lattice grows in frame.

Shot 2, exactly 4 seconds at 24 fps, GROUND LEVEL. After a hard cut, the camera stands among people at human eye height in the SAME city, in a completely different vantage point from shot 1. People go about ordinary daily life: walking, trading, carrying, eating, queueing. People read clearly from the middle ground outward, at full height and mostly from behind or in three-quarter view, hands occupied with baskets, tools, crates and cloth; the nearest stretch of the frame stays clear of any figure. Warm practical light from windows, stalls, lamps and cooking fires falls across the scene. Signs, boards, awnings and banners carry painted symbols, numerals-free colour fields and plain weave instead of words, so no lettering or logo is legible anywhere in frame. The same recognisable landmark stays readable somewhere in the background or on the horizon so the two shots read as one city. One slow, single-direction camera move only, at a constant height.

Ground level on the Champ de Mars at the foot of the tower, camera at eye height among the crowd. The planted iron lattice fills the background and rises out of the top of frame. A busy produce market runs across the gravel under canvas awnings, tables piled with greens, tomatoes, herbs and bread, and shoppers move between the stalls further in, seen from behind with baskets on their arms. Growers lower crates on a hoist from the first growing deck above. Late afternoon sun comes through the leaves and lands in warm patches on the tables. The camera glides forward slowly between the stalls at a constant height for the full duration.
